items.text: The children’s’ show ‘Thomas the Tank Engine’ has some big changes this year. Ian McCure, supervising producer, said that the stories have been around for 73 years. To launch the new series, there will be a new theme song, international characters and stories set around the world and in Sodor . There will also be the original characters, new characters, and the first female controller of the locomotives . Production of new toys also started, and people sell one around the world every minute! Difficult words: Sodor (an imaginary place in the ‘Thomas the Tank Engine’ stories), controller (the person who tells the trains where to go), locomotive (a powered rail vehicle that pulls trains). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The ‘Thomas the Tank Engine’ show has big changes this year. The producer said that the stories have been around for 73 years, so to launch the new show, there will be a new theme song, international characters, and stories set around the world and in Sodor . Original characters, new characters, and the first female controller of the trains will be in the show. People started to make new toys for the show, and people sell one around the world every minute! Difficult words: launch (start), Sodor (a made-up place in the ‘Thomas the Tank Engine’ stories), controller (the person who tells the trains where to go). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The ‘Thomas the Tank Engine ’ stories are around 73 years old. There is also a TV show about the stories. This year, there will be a new show. It will have a new theme song. It will have characters from around the world. The stories will be around the world and in Sodor . It will also have the first woman leader of the trains. People start to make new toys for the show. They are very popular! Difficult words: tank engine (a train engine that has a big container to hold oil or water so it can run), will (the future tense of ‘to be’), Sodor (a made-up place for the ‘Thomas the Tank Engine’ stories). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Kosovo was a Serbian province up until the 1990s when war between Albanians and Serbians broke out. In 1998, Serbia attacked Albanian separatists and killed over 10,000 people. This month, Albanian war veterans from Kosovo blocked roads to stop a visit by the Serbian president Vucic. They burned the tires and placed large logs and heavy machinery in the roads. One veteran said that he and the other soldiers stopped tanks from coming down this road, so there was no way that the president was going to come, either. Difficult words: province (an area in a country), separatist (someone who wants a part of a country to be its own country), heavy machinery (large vehicles for doing construction work). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Kosovo was a part of Serbia until the 1990s when war between Albanians and Serbians broke out. In 1998, Serbia killed over 10,000 people when it attacked Albanian separatists . This month, Albanian war veterans from Kosovo blocked roads to stop a visit by the Serbian president. They burned tires and placed big logs and vehicles in the roads. One veteran said that he and the other soldiers stopped tanks from coming down this road, so the president was not going to come, either. Difficult words: separatist (someone who wants a part of a country to be a new and free country), veteran (someone who fought in a war). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Kosovo is a part of Serbia until the 1990s. A war starts between Albanians and Serbians. Albanians separatists want to leave Serbia. Over 10,000 people die. This month, Albanian war veterans from Kosovo block roads. They want to stop a visit by the Serbian president. They burn tires . They put big pieces of wood and big cars in the roads. During the war, one veteran says that he and other soldiers stop tanks. He says that they can stop the president, also. Difficult words: separatist (someone who wants a part of a country to be a free country), veteran (someone who is in a war), tires (the ‘circles’ on a car that move the car). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Between 1998 and 2000, two East African countries named Eritrea and Ethiopia fought in a border war which killed thousands, and then closed the border. Earlier this year, Ethiopia fully embraced a peace deal and last Tuesday, the border reopened. Families could reunite for the first time in 20 years, embassies reopened, telephone lines restored, and commercial flights resumed. Politicians and hundreds of people from both of the countries celebrated the reopening of the two key crossing points. Difficult words: embrace (accept). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Between 1998 and 2000, two East African countries named Eritrea and Ethiopia fought in a border war. Thousands of people died and people closed the border. Earlier this year, Ethiopia fully accepted a peace deal. The border between the two countries reopened last Tuesday, and some families r eunited for the first time in 20 years. Embassies reopened, telephone lines restored, and commercial flights resumed. Politicians and hundreds of people celebrated the reopening of the border. Difficult words: border (the line between two countries), accept (say ‘yes’ to), reunite (come together). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Eritrea and Ethiopia are in East Africa. They share a border . Between 1998 and 2000, people there fight. Thousands of people die. People close the border. This year, Ethiopia accepts a peace deal . Now, the border is open. It is open for the first time in 20 years. People can meet again. People are happy about this. Hundreds of them celebrate. Difficult words: border (the line between two countries), accept (say ‘yes’ to), peace deal (a plan for peace – no fighting). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

NOAA (The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration) released images of Hurricane Florence moving across the Atlantic. Last week on Tuesday, it was moving towards the American states of North and South Carolina. When it hits, people expect it to reach a Category 5 strength with winds of up to 250 kilometres per hour. Authorities ordered more than 1 million people to evacuate coastal areas. Difficult words: release (show to people), expect (if people expect something to happen, they think that it is going to happen), Category 5 (a large hurricane). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

There are images of Hurricane Florence from space, as it moves across the Atlantic. Last week on Tuesday, it was moving towards the American states of North and South Carolina. When it hits, it will be a Category 5 hurricane, which means that its winds will blow up to 250 kilometres per hour. More than 1 million people evacuate to get away. Difficult words: evacuate (leave the area where you live to move to safety). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Hurricane Florence is a big storm. It is moving across the Atlantic. It is going to hit the USA. It will hit the states of North and South Carolina. When the hurricane hits, it will be a Category 5 hurricane. This means that its winds will blow 250 kilometres per hour. More than 1 million people evacuate to get away. Difficult words: be going to (in the future), will (in the future), evacuate (leave home and move to safety). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Since 2015, an influx of 1million refugees have come into Germany, which has made some people uneasy. In Chemitz, Germany, thousands of far-right protesters gathered in response to the alleged killing of a German citizen by Syrian and Iraqi migrants. Many supporters of the party called ‘Alternative for Germany’ wore all black clothing at the ‘mourning march’. Police had to intervene when the event became violent, and they tried to keep the protesters away from counter – demonstrators . About 2,000 people went to a separate protest in support of foreign sentiment . Difficult words: influx (when a lot of something comes all at once), far-right (people who are conservative, traditional, and want a country to stay the same), alleged (supposed), intervene (get involved), counter-demonstrator (a protester who protests against something that others protest), foreign sentiment (supporting immigrants). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Since 2015, an influx of 1 million immigrants have come into Germany, which has made some people uncomfortable. In Chemitz, Germany, thousands of protesters came together because of an alleged killing of a German by immigrants. Many protesters wore black at the ‘ mourning march ’. Police had to stop some of the protest when it became violent, and they tried to keep the protesters away from people who disagreed with them. About 2,000 people went to a different protest to support immigrants. Difficult words: influx (a lot), alleged (some people say that it is true), mourning march (when people march to support someone who died). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Since 2015, 1 million migrants move to Germany. This makes some people unhappy. In Chemitz, Germany, there is a killing. People say that immigrants kill a German citizen . Thousands of people come together to protest. They wear black. They hold a mourning march . People get violent during the protests. Police have to stop some people. There are also people who want to help immigrants. The police keep them away from the protesters. Difficult words: citizen (someone who is from a country and lives there for a long time), mourning march (when people walk together to show respect to someone who died), violent (when people attack each other). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In the Indian city of Kolkata, a 30-metre section of a highway overpass collapsed, trapping half a dozen vehicles. Firefighters used cutting tools to remove people from the cars, and seven or eight people went to hospital due to injuries. In 2016, also in Kolkata, another section of a highway overpass collapsed, leading to 26 deaths. Difficult words: overpass (a road/highway above other roads), a dozen (12), due to (because of). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Kolkata, India, a part of a highway overpass fell down and trapped about six vehicles . Firefighters cut the cars to save people, and some people went to hospital. In Kolkata in 2016, another section of a highway overpass fell down. Twenty-six people died then. Difficult words: overpass (a road/highway above other roads), vehicle (cars, trucks, bikes), trapped (not able to move). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Kolkata, India, part of a highway overpass falls down. It traps about six cars. Firefighters cut the cars open to save the people. Some people go to hospital. In Kolkata in 2016, another part of a highway overpass fell down. Twenty-six people died then. Difficult words: overpass (a ‘bridge’ – a highway which is above highway road), trap (covers under pieces of road – the people are in danger, they cannot move), fell (past of ‘fall’). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A powerful earthquake hit wide areas of Hokkaido last Thursday, which is Japan’s northernmost main island. The island’s largest city of Sapporo was hit at 3:08 a.m. The 6.7-magnitude quake injured over 150 people and killed at least seven. It triggered dozens of landslides, cracked roads and buried vehicles in several feet of mud. Almost three million people were left without electricity due to an emergency shut-down of the main power plant. The Japanese Prime Minister, Shinzo Abe, pledged to send 25,000 troops to assist rescue efforts. Difficult words: trigger (start), dozens (many), due to (because of), pledge (promise something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A powerful earthquake hit Hokkaido last Thursday, which is Japan’s northernmost main island. The island’s largest city Sapporo was hit at 3:08 a.m. The earthquake injured over 150 people, and seven people died. The earthquake triggered many landslides, cracked roads, and buried vehicles in mud. Almost three million people were left without electricity. The Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe said that he would send 25,000 soldiers to help with the rescue efforts . Difficult words: trigger (start), vehicle (cars, truck, motorbikes), rescue efforts (the actions of making things work again and saving people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

An earthquake hits Hokkaido, Japan. It is a powerful earthquake. It injures over 150 people. Seven people die. The earthquake starts landslides. Roads crack. Mud covers cars. Three million people are without electricity. Difficult words: earthquake (when the ground moves), powerful (very strong), mud (a mix of earth and water). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A colonial-era law in India held that homosexual acts were against the order of nature . Last Friday, the Supreme Court ruled to abolish the law, saying that discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation violated human rights. Many opponents of the former law gathered to celebrate outside the court. One of them said that gay people were finally free to be who they are in front of the law, which is all that they wanted. Media approached another person who said that this would open the doors for more civil rights . Difficult words: order of nature (when who you are as a person is a crime), rule (an order, officially and legally make something happen), abolish (stop), violate (break), former (not existing any more), gather (come together in large numbers), approach (ask), civil rights (people’s rights to be free). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A law in India made homosexual sex illegal. However, the Supreme Court there abolished the law last Thursday, and the court said that the law violated human rights . People came together outside the court and celebrated. One person said that gay people were free in front of the law. Another person said that this would open the doors for more civil rights. Difficult words: abolish (stop), violate (break), human rights (a peoples’ rights to be free). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is about a law . This law is in India. It makes sex between two women or between two men illegal . Now the law stops. The Supreme Court stops it. Some people celebrate outside the court. Difficult words: law (a rule – something which tells people what they can or must not do), illegal (if you do something illegal, the police can arrest you), Supreme Court (the highest, most powerful court). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

More than a million Japanese have been ordered to evacuate their homes as Typhoon Jebi approaches . It brings a160-kilometre-per-hour winds, and it is the strongest typhoon since 1993. Airports and train stations have been forced to close because of incoming water. The runway at the Kansai International Airport was left flooded and the cargo storage submerged . One of the most dramatic moments was when a tanker smashed into the side of a bridge. Difficult words: approach (come), submerged (covered under water), smash (hit with a lot of force). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

More than a million Japanese had to evacuate as Typhoon Jebi is coming. It brings 160-kilometre-per-hour winds, and it is the strongest typhoon since 1993. Airports and train stations are closed because of water. Water flooded t he runway at the Kansai International Airport. A big tanker even smashed into the side of a bridge. Difficult words: flooded (covered under water), tanker (a big ship which usually carries oil), smash (hit with a lot of force). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Typhoon Jebi is coming to Japan. A million Japanese must leave their homes. They are in danger. The typhoon brings 160-kilometre-per-hour winds. It is the strongest typhoon since 1993. Airports and train stations are closed. They are under water. A tanker smashes into a bridge. Difficult words: typhoon (a tropical storm), tanker (a big ship which usually carries oil), smash (hit very hard). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A massive fire tore through the 200-year-old National Museum of Brazil in Rio de Janeiro last Sunday. Firefighters worked through the night to combat the blaze in the north of the city, but people believe that more than 20,000 items related to the history of Brazil are destroyed. People do not yet know how the fire began, but staff had complained of the decrepit state of the building. The country’s president said that the day was a sad one for all Brazilians. Difficult words: tear (destroy, move though quickly), combat (fight), blaze (a very large fire), item (a thing, usually a special one), decrepit (old and in a bad state). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A massive fire tore thought the Museum of Brazil in Rio de Janeiro last Sunday. The museum is 200 years old, and it lost more than 20,000 items . Firefighters worked through the night to bring the fire under control. We do not know how the fire began. However, the building was old and not in a good state. Brazil’s president said that this was a sad day for all Brazilians. Difficult words: tear (destroy, move though quickly), item (a thing, usually a special one). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This is not good news. The Museum of Brazil is on fire. More than 20,000 items are lost. The museum is 200 years old. It is important for Brazil. Brazil’s president says that this is a sad day. We do not know how the fire starts. However, the building was old. It was not in a good state . Difficult words: item (a thing, usually a special one), was (past of ‘is’), state (a situation; in this story, the museum was not good). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Rock hyrax triplets were born recently at Chester Zoo on July 19. The babies weighed less than 250 grams, which is about the size of a mango. These small, furry mammals (which look a little like rabbits or badgers) have close relations to elephants despite their differences in size and appearance; one similarity is their two large incisors that grow like tusks . In the wild, the rock hyrax lives in Africa and the Arabian Peninsula in rocky terrain . The animals communicate with one another by making up to 20 different noises. Difficult words: incisor (a narrow tooth used for cutting), tusks (the very big ‘teeth’ of an elephant), terrain (land).

On July 19, three rock hyrax triplets were born at Chester Zoo in England. They weighed less than 250 grams. These furry little animals look a little like a rabbit. They are much smaller than elephants but they are related to them. One similarity is that their two large incisors grow like an elephant’s tusks . In the wild, the rock hyrax lives in Africa and in the Arabian Peninsula in rocky land. They also make up to 20 different noises to communicate with one another. Difficult words: furry (covered in fur – thick hair), be related to (be genetically similar in some way), incisor (a skinny tooth used for cutting), tusks (the very big ‘teeth’ of an elephant).

In July, rock hyrax triplets are born at Chester Zoo. They weigh less than 250 grams. The rock hyrax is a small animal. It looks like a rabbit. The rock hyrax is much smaller than an elephant. However, it is related to an elephant. It has two large incisors. Incisors are teeth; people have them, too. However, the rock hyrax has very big incisors. The elephant’s incisors grow so big that they become tusks. Tusks are very big incisors. That is why the rock hyrax is related to the elephant. In the wild , the rock hyrax lives in Africa and in the Middle East. It lives in rocky land. It also makes up to 20 different noises. It ‘talks’ with other rock hyrax with these noises. Difficult words: triplets (three babies born at the same time), to be related to (be similar in some way), in the wild (not in zoos or parks).

In Jacksonville, Florida, people were at a gaming bar to watch a video game football match and see the players when a gunman named David Katz came into the bar, shot two people, and then shot himself. Police reported that there were three deceased and nine injured people from bullet wounds; two people drove themselves to hospital. David Katz was 24 years old and from Baltimore. The FBI is investigating the shooting. Difficult words: deceased (dead). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Florida, people were at a gaming bar. They were there to meet players and watch the video game football match. A gunman came into the bar and opened fire , killing two and injuring nine people. He then shot himself. Police reported that two of the injured people drove themselves to hospital. The gunman was from Maryland and the FBI is helping the police investigate the shooting. Difficult words: gunman (a person who uses a gun to hurt or kill people), open fire (start shooting), investigate (find out more). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Florida, people are at a gaming bar. It is a bar where people play video games. Other people can watch them, talk, drink and eat. The gamers are playing a football video game. A gunman comes into the bar. He opens fire . He kills two people. He injures nine people. Then he shoots himself. Two injured people can drive. They drive themselves to hospital. The FBI is helping the police. They want to know more about the shooting and the gunman. Difficult words: gunman (a person who shoots a gun to hurt or kill people), open fire (start to shoot), shooting (when somebody shoots people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In the German State of Bavaria, not far from Ingolstadt, there was a huge explosion at an oil refinery. The explosion injured at least eight people while another 1,800 living close by temporarily evacuated due to potentially toxic smoke. The cause of the explosion is yet to be determined . The Bavarian Interior Minister spoke of luck at the site , as more people could have been injured in the incident, adding that the material damage was immense . Difficult words: huge (very big), temporarily (for some time), due to (because of), determine (find out), site (the place of the incident), immense (great). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Germany, there was a huge explosion at an oil refinery . The oil refinery is in the State of Bavaria, not far from the city of Ingolstadt. The explosion injured at least eight people, and another 1,800 temporarily had to evacuate. No one yet knows what caused the explosion. Difficult words: huge (very big), oil refinery (a ‘factory’ where people turn oil into petrol, wax or diesel oil), temporarily (for some time). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There is an explosion in Germany. It happens at an oil refinery . It is in the State of Bavaria. The explosion injures eight or more people. Another 1,800 people have to evacuate . We do not know why this explosion happens. Difficult words: oil refinery (a factory where people turn oil into petrol and other things), injure (when something bad happens to a person’s body), evacuate (move away because of danger). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Around 300 sea turtles died from asphyxiation or toxic algae after getting entangled in an illegal fishing net off Mexico’s southern Pacific coast. The turtles, of a species in danger of extinction , were buried in sand on a beach. An official said that the fishermen told them that the fishing net was local, adding that it could have been abandoned by a tuna fishing ship without reporting it was lost. Who set the illegal 120-metre net is being investigated and the guilty ones can face criminal charges. Difficult words: asphyxiation (death by not having oxygen), toxic algae (a simple water plant which produces toxins), entangled (caught), species (a kind of animal), extinction (dying out), abandon (leave behind). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Around 300 sea turtles got caught in an illegal fishing net off Mexico’s southern Pacific coast. All of them died from asphyxiation or toxic algae . They were buried in sand on a beach. Killing sea turtles is a crime in Mexico, and police are looking into who set the illegal 120-metre net. Fishermen said that the net was local. It is possible a tuna fishing ship abandoned it without telling anyone. Difficult words: asphyxiation (death by not having oxygen), toxic algae (a simple water plant which produces toxins – poison), abandon (leave behind). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There is an incident off Mexico’s southern Pacific coast . Somebody leaves a fishing net in the sea. Around 300 sea turtles get caught in the net. All of them die. People must not kill turtles in Mexico. It is a crime. Somebody can get in trouble for this. Difficult words: off (away from), coast (where the land touches the sea), fishing net (a material for catching fish). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The roof of the historical church of San Giuseppe dei Falegnami in central Rome collapsed last Thursday. People built it in the 16th century on the site of an ancient prison at the western edge of the Roman Forum. Luckily, the accident hurt no one as the church was closed to public when the roof fell. Firefighters only removed precious pieces of art while ensuring the structure was stable. Difficult words: precious (of great value and important), ensure (make sure). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The roof of a historical church in central Rome collapsed last Thursday. People built it in the 16th century on the site of an ancient prison at the western edge of the Roman Forum. Luckily, the accident hurt no one – the church was closed when the roof fell. Firefighters only removed pieces of art. Difficult words: collapse (fall down), site (a place), ancient (very old), remove (take away). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Rome, there is an accident. The roof of one church falls down. It is an old church. It is from the 16th century. When the roof falls down, no one is there. It is closed. No one is hurt. Firefighters only take away pieces of art. Difficult words: roof (the top part of a building). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A golden statue of Turkish President Erdogan was part of a ‘bad news’- themed art festival in Wiesbaden, a city in Germany. The statue was based on the statue of Saddam Hussein which the US army toppled in 2003. Authorities recently removed the four-metre effigy because, as they said, it provoked conflict by drawing pro and anti-Erdogan demonstrations. The artists behind the statue said that it started a public debate, so it fulfilled its purpose. Difficult words: themed (with the motive, topic), topple (knock down), authorities (the administration, the local government), effigy (a sculpture of a person). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Wiesbaden, a city in Germany, there was an art festival. Its theme was ‘bad news’, and one piece of art was a golden four-metre statue of Turkish President Erdogan. The statue drew pro and anti-Erdogan demonstrations. The German authorities say that it provoked conflict, so they decided to put it away. The artists behind the statue said that they only wanted to start a debate. Difficult words: theme (topic, motive, the thing the festival is about), draw (attract, make come), authorities (the administration, local government for example or ‘bosses’). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Wiesbaden is a city in Germany. There is an art festival. Its theme is ‘bad news’. There is a statue at the festival. It is gold. It is of Turkish President Erdogan. It is four metres tall. Some people support Erdogan. Some people do not. Pro-Erdogan and anti-Erdogan people come to the statue. Some of them protest, some of them cause trouble. The German authorities do not want trouble. They put the statue away. Difficult words: theme (an idea about something), support (say nice things about something), cause (make), authorities (the ‘bosses’ of the city). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Pope Francis travelled to Ireland last weekend in the first papal visit to the country since 1979 when Pope John Paul II drew crowds of 2.7 million. The current Pope expected to attract a fraction of that number (around 500,000) due to a series of scandals which undermined the once-powerful position of the Catholic Church. Beginning in the 1990s, a series of criminal cases established that hundreds of priests had abused thousands of children over decades. Police convicted six Irish priests between 1975 and 2001. The economic boom in the 1990s (which opened up Ireland to the world), the abortion referendum and legalising gay marriage also signalled changes in the nation’s attitude . Pope Francis met Ireland’s President Michael D. Higgins, and the head of government Leo Eric Varadkar at Dublin castle where they gave a speech. His Holiness expressed pain and shame at the failure of church authorities regarding the scandals. The historic visit to the country ended after the Holy Father attended a Mass in Dublin’s Phoenix Park where he begged forgiveness for the cases of sex abuse. Difficult words: papal (related to the Pope), due to (because of), attitude (the way people think about something), regarding (in connection to), Mass (the celebration of the Christian Eucharist). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Pope Francis travelled to Ireland last weekend in the first papal visit in 39 years. In 1979, Pope John Paul II drew crowds of 2.7 million. A series of scandals undermined the once-powerful position of the Catholic Church in Ireland. In the 1990s, people found out that hundreds of priests sexually abused thousands of children over many years. The 1990s were also the time when Ireland’s economy grew and opened the country to the world. The abortion referendum and legalising gay marriage also shows Ireland is in change. Pope Francis met Ireland’s President Michael D. Higgins, and the head of government Leo Eric Varadkar at Dublin castle where they gave a speech. The Pope expressed pain and shame over the scandals and asked for forgiveness . Difficult words: papal (related to the Pope), undermine (ruin, hurt, make weaker), abuse (do bad things to somebody), forgiveness (ask to forgive – no longer feel angry). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Pope John Paul II visits Ireland in 1979. Around 2.7 million people come to see him. A lot of people in Ireland like the Catholic Church in 1979. However, things change. Irish priests sexually abuse children. Hundreds of priests and thousands of children have this happen. People are angry. They stop liking the Catholic Church. Pope Francis visits Ireland this month in 2018. Only 500,000 people come to see him. He talks about the scandals . He is sad about them. Difficult words: priest (a man who is in a church, talk to people and organises events of the Church), abuse (do bad things to somebody), scandal (a bad event, something which makes people angry). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Maracaibo is city in Venezuela, has been experiencing rolling blackouts for months, as the country endures its worst ever-economic downturn. One housewife said that there were about 16–18 hours of blackouts a day during the week. With no electricity, it is impossible to refrigerate food, and some shoppers have resorted to buying spoiled meat. The media approached one shopper at a market and he said that the meat was no good, but he did not know what to do except to leave things to God’s will. He added that the meat smelled a little foul , but rinsing it with a little vinegar and lemon would do . The governor of the affected Venezuelan state said that the blackouts were being repaired, yet they persist . Difficult words: endure (suffer through something difficult), resort to (turn to doing something because of a serious situation), spoiled (that has gone bad), approach (ask), foul (bad), would do (work instead of something else), affected (experiencing a situation), persist (go on, still exist). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Venezuela is experiencing its worst-ever economic down turn , and the city of Maracaibo has had no electricity for months. One housewife said that there were about 16–18 hours without electricity a day during the week. Without electricity, people cannot keep their food cool in a fridge, and some shoppers buy spoiled meat. One man at a market said that the meat was not good but he bought it anyway. He did not know what to do about the situation, so he left it to God. He said that the meat smelled bad, but he planned to wash it with a little vinegar and lemon. Difficult words: experience (when you experience something, something happens to you), economic down turn (when the economy is bad – people have less money and do less business), spoiled (bad). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Venezuela has big problems. The economic situation there is very bad. One city has no electricity for months. People cannot use their fridges . They cannot keep their food cold and fresh. Their meat goes bad. Some people buy bad meat anyway . One shopper buys the meat. He plans to wash it with vinegar and lemon. Difficult words: economic (how much money people have, what shops have, etc.), fridge (a machine which keeps your food cold), anyway (if you do something anyway, you do it even though it is a bad idea). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The US federal authorities discovered a drug- smuggling tunnel between the USA and Mexico in an abandoned KFC restaurant. The tunnel leads from a house in Mexico to the former fast-food restaurant in Arizona. Scott Brown from Homeland Security Department said that criminals smuggled a very significant quantity of hard narcotics across the border. So far, police arrested the restaurant’s owner after police found packages of Class A drugs in his truck, but the authorities aim to identify everybody involved in the undertaking as the construction of the tunnel in itself was a crime. Difficult words: smuggle (move something illegally to another country), abandoned (no longer used), former (ex-), Homeland Security Department (a part of government which makes sure people are safe), significant (great), narcotic (a drug that people use for pain or dulling sensation), Class A (most dangerous), undertaking (activity). Police discovered a drug- smuggling tunnel between the USA and Mexico. It leads from a house in Mexico to an abandoned KFC restaurant in the USA. Police say that criminals smuggled large amounts of hard drugs across the border. Police arrested the restaurant’s owner, but they want to find everybody who had something to do with the business. Building the tunnel is in itself a crime. Difficult words: discover (find), smuggle (illegally move something to another country), abandoned (no longer used). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Police find a tunnel. It is on the border between the USA and Mexico. It starts in a house in Mexico. It leads to a KFC restaurant in the USA. The restaurant is old and closed. This is a tunnel for smuggling drugs. Police arrest the KFC’s owner . However, they want to find more guilty people. Making a tunnel between the USA and Mexico is a crime. Difficult words: border (the line between two countries), smuggle (move something illegal to another country), owner (a person who owns – has something), guilty (a person guilty of a crime does/did the crime). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Great Britain, the government is targeting puppy farms to ensure animal welfare in its new plans to ban third-party sales of puppies and kittens. Michael Gove, the Environment Secretary, said that there is a big problem in Britain (and in Europe) with puppy farming because, at the moment, there are thousands of animals brought up in horrendous conditions and their lives are blighted . The ban means that pet shops and other commercial dealers will no longer be able to sell kittens or puppies, and those looking for a pet under 6 months old will have to deal with breeders or rescue centres. Difficult words: target (visit and see if everything is OK), welfare (health and happiness), horrendous (terrible), blighted (ruined). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The British government is targeting puppy farms to ensure animal welfare . One politician said that there is a big problem in Britain (and in Europe as well) with puppy farming. Many of the animals are brought up in terrible conditions and their lives are ruined. There is going to be a new law – pet shops will not be able to sell kittens or puppies under 6 months old. Difficult words: target (visit and see if everything is OK), ensure (make sure), welfare (health and happiness). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is from Britain. Many young dogs and cats are live in terrible conditions . The British government wants to stop this. They want to make sure that the animals are fine and healthy. They visit and check puppy farms. There is a new law, also. Pet shops cannot sell animals under 6 months old. Difficult words: terrible (very bad), conditions (a situation, a place), government (the ‘bosses’ of a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
